title: COVID-19 mRNA Vaccine-Associated Myocarditis Presenting as STEMI in a 48-Year-Old Male.
ehr_evidence: The data used to support the findings of this study are included within the article. This is a single-patient case report based on clinical documentation (history, physical exam, EKG, cardiac catheterization, and laboratory results) collected during routine care rather than an electronic health record database analysis.
summary: Case report of a 48-year-old Hispanic male who developed COVID-19 mRNA (Moderna) vaccine-associated myocarditis presenting as STEMI shortly after his second vaccine dose, with normal coronaries, reduced ejection fraction (40%), elevated troponin, and rapid symptom resolution.
key_findings: The patient had elevated troponin (4.40 ng/mL at presentation, peak 13.60 ng/mL) and CRP 5.10 mg/dL with normal patent coronary arteries on angiography and estimated ejection fraction of 40% with anterolateral and apical hypokinesis.
Nasopharyngeal SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR and respiratory viral panel were both negative.
Chest pain and flu-like symptoms resolved with trending-down troponins and CRP; at 3-month follow-up the patient was asymptomatic on guideline-directed medical therapy.
A history of viral myocarditis 7 years prior was noted, but it remains unclear whether this is a predisposing factor to mRNA vaccine-associated myocarditis.
population: Single 48-year-old male in a US emergency/cardiac care setting
limitations: Single case report with no generalizability or control group.
Cardiac MRI was unavailable and endomyocardial biopsy was not performed, limiting definitive diagnosis.
Prior viral myocarditis as a predisposing factor is unconfirmed.
Short follow-up (3 months) with no long-term or recurrence data.
data_availability_statement: The data used to support the findings of this study are included within the article.
